steps.name: Library sizes, normalization, PCA, sample-distance matrix
caveats: Do not run any differential expression test in this step — this is QC only

sample_01's low library size can distort size-factor estimation in DESeq2-style normalization; check whether excluding it changes size factors materially and note this rather than silently accepting a skewed factor
With only 12000 genes and 12 samples, PCA is being computed in a low-n regime — do not over-interpret components beyond PC1/PC2 without checking explained variance
12 samples is a small n for correlation-based distance stability; report distances descriptively rather than testing significance of clustering
steps.question: Across the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples), what are the per-sample library sizes, how do samples separate on a PCA of variance-stabilized/normalized expression, and what does the sample-to-sample distance (or correlation) matrix show about clustering by condition versus outlier behavior — with particular attention to sample_01, flagged as having a library size about 4x below the median?

grounding.reason: No knowledge_recommend tool was attached in this session; standard bulk RNA-seq QC practice (size factors, vst/rlog, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) applied directly to the profiled counts and metadata.

acceptance_criteria: Reports raw library size (total counts) per sample from counts.csv, ranked, with the median and sample_01's ratio to median stated explicitly
Counts are normalized/variance-stabilized (e.g., DESeq2 vst or rlog, or size-factor + log-CPM) before PCA and distance computation, with the method named
PCA is computed on the normalized matrix and at least PC1 vs PC2 (with % variance explained) is reported, samples labeled by condition (AD lesional vs control) and sample ID

A full 12x12 sample-to-sample distance or correlation matrix (e.g., Euclidean distance on vst counts, or Spearman/Pearson correlation) is computed and summarized, e.g. via hierarchical clustering or a heatmap-equivalent table

Sample_01's position is explicitly reported in all three diagnostics: library size rank, PCA coordinates/distance from condition centroid or other samples, and its row/column in the distance matrix versus its nearest and farthest neighbors
Gene count filtering (if any, e.g. removing all-zero genes) prior to normalization is stated
Output includes per-sample numeric tables (library size, PCA coordinates, distance-matrix summary) suitable for the next step to interpret, not just plots

steps.name: QC synthesis and verdict on sample_01
caveats: This step must not introduce new computation beyond what T1S1 produced — it interprets those numeric outputs
Avoid recommending a hard-and-fast exclusion rule based on library size alone without corroborating it against the PCA/distance evidence from T1S1
steps.question: Given the library-size ranking, PCA structure, and sample-to-sample distance matrix computed for the 12 AD-lesional-vs-control skin samples, does sample_01's low library size (~4x below median) correspond to a genuine outlier in expression space, and what is the concrete recommendation (keep as-is, flag and proceed with sensitivity check, downweight, or exclude) before proceeding to differential expression?

grounding.reason: Interpretive synthesis step with no external method dependency; grounded directly in T1S1's numeric outputs.

acceptance_criteria: States explicitly whether sample_01 is an outlier on PCA (e.g., distance from its condition group's centroid relative to other samples of the same condition) and on the sample-distance matrix (e.g., is it the most dissimilar sample to all others, or only mildly so)

Distinguishes the observation (low library size) from the interpretation (whether this manifests as expression-level distortion) from the recommendation (what to do about it) — does not conflate a low count depth with an automatic quality failure

Gives a specific, actionable verdict: e.g. exclude sample_01 from downstream DE, retain with a note to check DE result sensitivity by excluding it, or retain as unremarkable if PCA/distance show it clustering normally with its condition group

If condition balance would be affected by excluding sample_01 (currently 6 vs 6), states the resulting design (e.g. 5 vs 6) and flags that this is an unpaired design already, so removal does not break pairing but does reduce power in one arm
Does not overclaim — if the diagnostics are ambiguous (e.g., low depth but no PCA outlier signal), states that explicitly rather than forcing a binary verdict

plan.title: AD skin RNA-seq: QC, PCA, sample distances
plan.analytical_narrative: This is a pre-testing QC pass on a 12-sample (6 AD lesional vs 6 control), single-batch bulk RNA-seq dataset (12000 x 12 raw Salmon gene counts) with one flagged caveat: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. Before any differential expression is run, we need to characterize library sizes, normalize and variance-stabilize the counts, examine global sample structure by PCA, and quantify sample-to-sample similarity via a distance matrix / hierarchical clustering, then render an explicit verdict on whether sample_01 should be flagged, downweighted, or excluded going forward. All of this is a single cohesive QC task on one count matrix, so it is one track on the bulk-transcriptomics-agent, split into two dependent steps: (1) library-size + normalization/variance-stabilization + PCA + sample-distance computation, and (2) a synthesis step that interprets those diagnostics into a concrete verdict on sample_01 and overall cohort quality. No differential expression, enrichment, or reference data is invoked here since the question is purely descriptive QC on the count matrix and metadata already provided.
